definition: ChatScript is a combination Natural Language engine and dialog management system designed initially for creating chatbots, but is currently also used for various forms of NL processing.
details: It is written in C++. The engine is an open source project at SourceForge. and GitHub. ChatScript was written by Bruce Wilcox and originally released in 2011, after Suzette (written in ChatScript) won the 2010 Loebner Prize, fooling one of four human judges.

explainer.lead: ChatScript is an open-source C++ system that combines natural-language processing with dialog management. It was created for building chatbots, but can also support other kinds of language processing.

tiers.eli5: ChatScript is like both a listener and a conversation director for a computer program. One part helps make sense of what someone says, while the other helps decide what the program should say next. Although it was first made for chatbots, it can help with other language tasks too.
tiers.practitioner: Use ChatScript when you want a natural-language engine and dialog management in one C++ system. Its open-source project is available on SourceForge and GitHub. Keep the tool separate from applications built with it: Suzette was a chatbot written in ChatScript, not another name for the engine.
tiers.paperLevel: ChatScript can be described as a C++ software system combining a natural-language engine with dialog management: input language is processed to produce conversational replies or other natural-language-processing output. It was written by Bruce Wilcox and originally released in 2011, after Suzette, written in ChatScript, won the 2010 Loebner Prize by fooling one of four human judges.

explainer.example: A support chatbot could receive “Where is my order?”, process the sentence with ChatScript's natural-language engine, and use its dialog management to continue the order-tracking conversation by asking for an order number.

usedIn.name: Suzette

usedIn.name: Chatbot development

usedIn.name: Natural-language processing
usedIn.detail: ChatScript is also used for forms of language processing beyond chatbots.

explainer.intuition: A useful chatbot needs both language understanding and control over the conversation. ChatScript brings those two jobs together instead of treating them as entirely separate systems.
howItWorks: The natural-language engine processes that text.
The dialog management system determines the conversational response.
The system produces a reply or another language-processing result.
explainer.whyItMatters: ChatScript offers a single open-source foundation for both interpreting language and managing dialog. Its use in Suzette also connects it to a chatbot that fooled one of four human judges in the 2010 Loebner Prize.
misconceptions: ChatScript is not limited to chatbots; it is also used for other natural-language processing.
Suzette is not ChatScript itself; Suzette was a chatbot written in ChatScript.

diagram.caption: ChatScript combines natural-language processing and dialog management in one system.
